program: Therapeutic school, day treatment and family mental-health support
priceScope: Matched FY2025 full annual recipient cost against conditional school/day-treatment clinical and caregiver resources; not whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Tennyson provides a therapeutic K–12 school and day treatment for children with complex behavioral and emotional needs.
It also offers child and family therapy, parenting support and community-based services across Colorado.
Its TREE program supports young adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities preparing for more independent lives.
strengths: Intensive school-based clinical, family and educational support addresses children with high needs.
A current report provides a dated 63-student school-served envelope and 17 community-school transitions.
Original child-trauma trials provide a plausible clinical mechanism without assuming measured local utility.
reservations: School-served students are not documented completed clinical doses or causal successes.
Utility, eligible case mix, caregiver net resources and provider contribution remain judgments.
The whole annual recipient cost covers several important unquantified channels beyond the modeled school subset.

sections.what: Tennyson’s therapeutic school and day treatment combine special education, individual/group/family therapy, occupational and speech supports. School placement requires a district-approved IEP separate-school setting. Its statewide community services include outpatient family therapy and PCIT; current PCIT ages 2–7 usually involves approximately 20 sessions, a dose not automatically supplied to every school student. TREE adds independent living and employment preparation but does not establish net wage gains.
sections.monitoring: FY 2025 annual report page 2 says school/day treatment served 63 children, compared with 46 in FY 2024, and 17 returned to community schools. Nearly 1000 children ANDfamilies is a mixed-unit statement, not a unique patient denominator. Reported reading/math improvements are pre/post educational outcomes, not controlled health utility. Next useful evidence is unique completed clinical dose, clinical case mix, local residence, caregiver work/time and active-provider comparison.
sections.qualitative: The original Cohen randomized trial assigned 229 sexually abused children 8–14 with PTSD symptoms to TF-CBT or child-centered therapy and found better child symptoms and caregiver outcomes. It did not measure a QALY conversion, and Tennyson’s broader trauma-informed/ARC/neurodevelopmental programs and autism/IDDcase mix differ. The .5 compatible clinical subgroup and .03 one-year utility (10.95 healthy-day equivalents) are explicitly conditional hypotheses, not imported empirical effectiveness. Public school placements and covered therapists form an active alternative. PCIT abuse-recurrence evidence is not extrapolated to all school children.
sections.cost: Full FY 2025 IRS recipient expense is$ 11,829,871 including$ 171,197 netted direct fundraising cost. A separate$ 5,825,981 recognized school/day-treatment program-cost sensitivity is source-aligned but excludes allocated administration, fundraising and unrecognized resource costs; it is not a marginal-gift price. Clinical patient health is not reduced by household grouping. Caregiver households use .9 household factor, .2 incremental provider share, .5 clinical-compatible subgroup and .5 net-resource response, with$ 500 after-tax/benefit/work/childcare resource gain as a judgment—not child wages. Positive gains alone receive 50%overlap adjustment; all households retain$ 10 incremental access/timecost and all students retain process harms. Resource gains and costs share one household log. Residential, community, PCIT, TREE and educational welfare remain unknown, not zero.
sections.funding: The legal recipient is Tennyson Center for Children at Colorado Christian Home, DBA Tennyson Center for Children, EIN 61-1458290. Original full FY 2025/FY 2024/FY 2023 IRS expenses are$ 11,829,871/$ 13,581,906/$ 11,112,242; mean$ 12,174,673. Annual report financial totals differ from the IRS totals; no reconciliation is claimed. Current giving links to the recipient’s ColoradoGives profile; no donation executed. Public education payments, Medicaid and private-pay alternatives matter; restricted additional donor capacity remains unmeasured. Distinct public-provider loss and unrecognized external resource costs are tested, not presumed absent.

model.costScope: Full latest FY2025 recipient expenses plus netted fundraising costs; partial school benefit reference and observed school-only recognized-cost sensitivity.
model.geographicAttribution: Denver school benefits use judged .9resident share within ten-county CBSA19740, not headquarters or all statewide community clients.
model.formula: Health=(Npatients × compatible clinical subgroup × dose × provider contribution × finite expected clinical utility − full patient harms) × local share. Household resources use N × household grouping with gated caregiver gains; same-year full costs and gains jointly logged, distinct payer costs localized once. Price=10C/(health+signed resource equivalent).
model.counterfactual: Publicly funded special-education placements, other trauma/family therapists and covered services without Tennyson integration.
model.attribution: Judged .2incremental recipient contribution versus active alternatives, independent of clinical-compatible subgroup and dose; no automatic next-gift expansion.
model.uncertainty: Local utility, fidelity, completed dose, parent net earnings, household duplication, geographic share and omitted portfolio channels remain unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: FY2025 school/day-treatment served63children,17community-school transitions; nearly1000children and families overall is mixed units and not summed.
